utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Madam Registrar. And good morning, everybody. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record all the accused are present. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Bourgon. I think that's about it. From the Prosecution, I notice the presence of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. All right. I understand that you have some preliminaries that you wish to discuss, debate, or raise. We were informed in the first place that you asked, I don't know who, asked for further submissions on the Borovcanin -- yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, good morning. Mr. Lazarevic and I have been discussing the matter and we are going to -- planning on to talking after court today, and we'll get back to you as soon as we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let me go through some preliminaries myself. It seems that you are encountering problems, Mr. McCloskey, to bring in a witness on the 11th and on the 12th. Is that still the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. In case it remains the position, then we are calling on you, when I say you, it's both sides, of course, to prepare yourselves for oral submissions during Wednesday -- the sitting of Wednesday, the 11th, relating to the issue that you raised, the Prosecution, in other words, namely relating to the question as to whether you have the right to -- or should be allowed to interview prospective Defence witnesses. So it's not something new to this Tribunal. It has been debated and decided upon on a few occasions, including by myself. So but of course, circumstances vary from case to case and from witness to witness, and we would be ready to hear your oral submissions this Wednesday at 9.00 in the morning when we sit. That's unless we still have an overflow of -- is it in the afternoon? Okay, sorry. I think it's in the morning but -- anyway, Wednesday -- the Wednesday sitting whatever time it is, unless of course we still have evidence spilling over to that day, in which case first we'll finish the evidence and then we have the submissions. Without -- if it is not possible to have the submissions on the 11th, we will have them on the 12th. All right? There is a motion by the Prosecution for leave to amend the 65 ter exhibit list with 18 exhibits pertaining to Alistair Graham. This was filed on the 6th of July. According to the information that we've -- that has been provided to us, this gentleman is due to testify on the 18th of July. That's pretty near. So we are fixing a time limit on the Defence to file their response. This will be due by not later than the end of business on Thursday, 12th July. All right? Then there is this confidential Defence motion on behalf of Drago Nikolic which has been joined now by others, requesting the Trial Chamber to order the Prosecution to urgently disclose all Rule 68 material related to witnesses PW 108 and PW 102. As I said, this was joined by the Defence team of Ljubisa Beara. We are telling you what -- because we are not exactly digesting well this kind of procedure, so we are not going to mince words on it. Disclosure obligations are provided or -- and articulated by the rules. They are clear for everyone, and each party should know what its disclosure obligations are, and it's not for the Trial Chamber to be seized with motions to tell the other party what its obligations are. So since Witness PW-108 is due to testify on the 17th of July, and this is pretty near, we are proposing that you, Mr. McCloskey, inform the Nikolic and Beara teams today if the evidence they are seeking falls under Rule 68, and that if it does fall, then that it should be provided by you without the need for a motion. Our position is that a motion would only be required if the application of Rule 68 is contested by the Prosecution. So our position is that the matter can be resolved through a dialogue which we expect you to have today between you, Mr. McCloskey, or someone delegated by you, and the Nikolic and the Beara team. And then you come back to us with the final solution. There is also another motion filed by the Prosecution for leave to amend the 65 ter exhibit list with intercepts or corroborating documents. I would enjoin the Defence teams, if possible, to come back with their response on this by the end of this week, by the end of this week. Thank you. Any further preliminary matters that you would like to raise? Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just to clarify while I have all Defence counsel. I think part of the motion you just mentioned, we had cited the Obrenovic and Trkulja statements. We did not -- we are not suggesting that those entire statements would come in as corroborating material but just particular portions where they talk about particular intercepts, and I'm not sure if that was made clear. Some Defence counsel may have thought we were trying to offer the entire statements but we were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I went through the list this morning with our Senior Legal Officer. I don't think I got the -- that impression. So the Defence might have got the wrong impression, too. Okay. I think we can bring in the witness. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, good morning, Your Honours, good morning, everyone. There are no measures being sought for this witness and a caution, I believe, would be in order from the Bench, Mr. President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Pepic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving evidence. Before you do so, our rules require to make a solemn declaration that you will be telling us the truth. So please take the text of that solemn declaration, read it out loud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us, which is equivalent of an oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness answered through interpreter].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Pepic. Please make yourself comfortable. Take a seat. General Pandurevic, are you able to follow the proceedings? THE ACCUSED PANDUREVIC: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure because I see that your headphones are not exactly where they should be. Yes, Mr. Pepic. You are going to be asked a number of questions, first by Mr. Thayer for the Prosecution, and then by members of the Defence teams. But before you -- we start with this process, I wish to alert you to a right, procedural right, that you have, which I'll try to explain in lay terms for you to be able to understand better. There may, although I'm not suggesting that there will, there may be some questions put to you which, if you were to answer truthfully, could possibly tend to expose you to criminal proceedings, we call these incriminatory questions. By law, you have a right, when such questions are put to you, to attract our attention, draw our attention, and ask us to exempt you from answering such questions. This is a right that you have to ask. You don't have an absolute right for such exemption. It depends on our discretion. We will evaluate all submissions and then we will come to a conclusion whether to grant you such exemption or whether to force you, compel you, to answer such a question. If, however, we force you to answer such questions, then whatever you state in your answer cannot be used against you in any future proceedings, criminal proceedings, unless you have made a false statement, in which case the proceedings will be for perjury. Then whatever you would have stated will not be covered by this privilege. Is this -- have I put it clear enough for you -- to you or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, he's all yours, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you state your name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Milenko Pepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how old are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber where you were born and raised?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was born in a place called Pepici, Kladanj municipality, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you identify yourself as a Bosnian Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how are you currently employed, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I'm a policeman by occupation. I work in Bratunac, in a centre for dog handling and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And approximately how long have you been doing that particular job?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I have been working there since 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And prior to that, what was your employment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Before that, I worked at the police station in Zvornik for a year, a year or so, maybe a little more than a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you some questions about your service history during the war and I'll just summarise it briefly. Please correct me if I've misstated anything or if you feel the need to add anything that I've forgotten, please do so. Essentially, sir, between April of 1992 and March of 1993, you served in the Sekovici Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You then joined the 2nd Sekovici Detachment of the Republika Srpska MUP Special Police Brigade in March of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And your detachment was headquartered in the Lovnica hotel in Sekovici, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it also correct that you served in the 2nd Sekovici Detachment essentially through the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention to 1995 and specifically the month of June of that year. Who was the commander of the Sekovici Detachment, and I'll just referred to the 2nd Sekovici Detachment as the Sekovici Detachment from now on, if that's okay. Who was the commander of that detachment in June of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Until mid-June 1995, the commander was Milos Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was he replaced at some point, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: By Rade Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was Mr. Cuturic known by a nickname?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was that nickname, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: His nickname was Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know why Mr. Stupar was replaced?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When Mr. Stupar was commanding your detachment, who was his immediate superior, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There was a special commander of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "special commander of the brigade," sir, who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, it was Goran Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Saric have anybody directly below him, sir, in a command position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: His deputy, and all the other detachment commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was his deputy's name, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: If I remember well, it was Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, is there any doubt in your mind as to who the deputy commander of the Special Police Brigade was in June and July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, it was Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in July of 1995, your detachment was divided into how many platoons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There were three platoons.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were they identified by number, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There was the 1st Platoon, the 2nd Platoon and the 3rd Platoon, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who led the 1st Platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was Marko Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in June of -- and July of 1995, who led the 2nd Platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 2nd Platoon was Jelenko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point, was Mr. Lukic incapacitated or taken out of action?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Approximately when was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but it was around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was he actually replaced with anyone or did the 2nd Platoon remain without a formal platoon leader?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. There was no commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, which platoon were you in?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the 2nd Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So with Mr. Lukic out of action, from whom did you and your platoon receive its orders in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We received orders directly from our detachment commander, Mr. Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was the leader or commander of the 3rd Platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Cop, Milenko, Cop. Milenko Trifunovic was the commander of that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was the 3rd Platoon known by any other name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: They were a platoon in Skelani, a forward platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So was it also referred to as the Skelani Platoon, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you describe, please, the uniforms that you and your detachment wore in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We had camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the -- or what were the predominant colours in that camouflage, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, green and a sort of coffee colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was the design of the uniform? By that, I mean was it a two-piece or a one-piece?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: These fatigues were in one piece.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did your detachment wear any emblem or insignia?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you wear it and what did it look like?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we wore these insignia on our left shoulders, left sleeve. They were black and they had a flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, sir, you yourself, what kind of equipment did you carry in the field? What kind of equipment and weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally I had my fatigues, I had a combat jacket, I had an automatic rifle, I had four clips, and two grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what types of mechanised weaponry or vehicles did your detachment have in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We had a bus, one bus, we had two lorries, one was a 110 lorry, the other 150 lorry. We also had a passenger vehicle, or one or two passenger vehicles. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in terms of mechanised weaponry or armoured vehicles, sir, what did your detachment have at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We had a tank, and we had a Praga.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you also have a three-barrelled anti-aircraft gun or cannon, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did your detachment have mortar support, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And finally, how about hand held rockets, zoljas, for example, did members of your detachment carry or use those on operations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, during the war, what was -- just generally, tell the Trial Chamber what the nature of your detachment's assignments was.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you just describe the nature of the activities that you performed when you were deployed in the field? How would you describe just the general nature of what you were doing when you were deployed in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were involved in combat activity. We secured the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you give the Trial Chamber just briefly the names of some theatres or battlefields to which you were deployed? No dates, just some names.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we were in the Sarajevo battlefield; throughout the Republika Srpska area, we were on Ozren and Majevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And during your deployment, sir, which senior Special Brigade, Special Police Brigade, commanders would you see in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There was Mr. Saric, the commander would come, and Mr. Borovcanin's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The translation we received, sir, was Mr. Saric would come and Mr. Borovcanin's deputy. Is that correct, that it was Mr. Borovcanin's deputy that would -- you would see in the field? Or would you see Mr. Borovcanin in the field?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, the deputy of Mr. Saric.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I just wanted to clarify that for the record. Okay, sir, I want to turn your attention now to some specific periods in July of 1995. At some point, you were deployed in the Sarajevo area. Can you tell the Trial Chamber more specifically where, what region?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were around Srednje. That's the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during that deployment, were all three of your detachments, platoons, deployed there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point, were you ordered to withdraw from that area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date on which you received that order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 11th of July, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you go, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We then set off in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that was, just to be clear, the same day, the 11th of July, that you set out, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was your final destination and approximately what time did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac, we were sent to the place called Bjelovac. It was quite late. It was after midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And during that night, sir, do you recall whether your platoon was the only one there or whether the other detachment platoons arrived as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The other platoons were up there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That brings us to the 12th of July, sir. Would you please tell the Trial Chamber what you did that morning?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, that morning we got up, we lingered there for a while, I don't know for how long, and then we were sent off in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you go from there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From Bratunac, we were sent towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you end up, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We ended up at a place in front of Potocari, before Potocari, near the Zuti Most or the Yellow Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you arrived at Zuti Most, did you see, or do you recall seeing any other MUP, VRS or Dutch army units there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember having seen them around the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what orders did you receive at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, if you look towards Potocari from Zuti Most, we were supposed to set out and clear the terrain, comb the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in what direction did you head, sir, just roughly speaking?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, if you look from Zuti Most in the direction of Potocari, it would be to the right. There was a hill of some sort up there and there were some villages there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate for the Trial Chamber the distance you travelled during your search of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, in my assessment, it was over a kilometre. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as you searched the terrain, sir, were you able to actually get a view of the UN base in Potocari at any time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What were you able to see there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I saw a building with a UN base. There were people in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you able to see any civilians gathering at the base, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was possible to observe the presence of civilians. There was a large group there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How close did you actually get to the UN base or to the main road which runs in front of it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were in front of the base, to the right, from the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, if I my colleague could read out the answer that we received because I believe this is not what the witness said because here it says "we were in front of the base."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand my friend's question? We have your answer as "we were in front of the base to the right from Zuti Most." Is that what you meant to say or did you say something else?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say that from the Zuti Most we set off to the right. We weren't, how should I put it, we weren't next to the UN base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. What were you are told to do in case you encountered anyone during the search of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We didn't encounter anyone during the search.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, my question was, sir, what were you are told to do in the event that you did encounter anyone, be it a civilian or a military-aged person who was surrendering? What were you told to do with such people?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, to inform our superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you directed in such an event to direct those individuals to any particular location, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, first we were to inform the officer and then he would issue further orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what is your recollection as to where such persons, who were encountered during the search, were to be directed or taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was already asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes [sic], and I think so too -- Mr. Thayer, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not that critical an issue, but I don't believe he actually answered the question I asked. I asked a slightly different question as to his understanding of where ultimately these people were going to be taken, whether he was the person that took them there or not. His answer was that his superior was going to do something and issue further orders. I'm just simply asking whether he understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Fair enough. Go ahead. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, again, what was your understanding as to where any individuals who were encountered in the field were going to be sent or taken?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, probably down there, in front of the UN base, as far as I -- as far as I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was giving you these instructions and this information, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We received instructions from our immediate superior, from the detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that was Mr. Cuturic, sir, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was he present with you during the search of this terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, he was there, as he was actually with us up there, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, on the occasions where you could see down to the UN base, did you see any Muslim men being separated from their families?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim men being detained?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims at all being boarded on to buses?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever see a large number of buses and trucks arrive from the direction of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes, but that was later.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, sir, and your testimony is, you didn't see any Muslims boarding those buses, but you did see some buses from the direction of Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, empty buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How long would you estimate that you spent searching the terrain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, probably more than an hour, an hour and a half, or two hours. Perhaps even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And at some point I take it you withdrew from that area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did you do next?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We went down to the vicinity of the Zuti Most and we got into our vehicles and we were sent off in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what were you told your next assignment was going to be, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we were to set off in the direction of Zvornik, and we were told we would be deployed in the place called Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what were you are told that you would be doing in this place called Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were to secure the road from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Secure the road from whom or from what, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we were told that there were Muslim forces, that the Muslim army, that the Muslim troops, had set off from the direction of Srebrenica and they were trying to break through in the direction of Tuzla. There was concern because it was thought that the road could be cut off to the place called Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from whom were you receiving this information and these orders?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We received orders from Mr. Cuturic, our commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So where did the bus actually take you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, we arrived in Kravica settlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So tell the Trial Chamber, please, what happened when you got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: When we got off, we set off in the direction of Sandici, and then we started deploying along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time of the day this was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps in the afternoon, as far as I can remember. I can't remember what time it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber, please, the order of the platoon deployment, to the best of your recollection, say, from Kravica, moving in the direction of Sandici? Can you just tell the Trial Chamber to the best of your recollection; for example, which platoon was closest to the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, first came the 2nd Platoon, then the 1st Platoon, and then over there, there was the 3rd Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear -- I'm sorry, sir, let me let you finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: That's what I remember the deployment to have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to clarify one thing. So, sir, is it your testimony, then, that the 3rd Platoon would have been located the closest of your detachment to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe at all the location at which you personally were deployed, if there was any feature or structure, and can you tell the Trial Chamber, in your estimation, approximately how far that was from the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I was by the road.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How far it was from Kravica, I can't say, because that's exactly where the confrontation -- that's exactly where the line between Kravica and Sandici lies, these two villages are next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sir, when the bus drove you from the Potocari area that day, before it dropped you off in Kravica, did it pass the warehouse, the Kravica warehouse, also known as the agricultural cooperative?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So do you have any estimation you can give the Trial Chamber for approximately how far from the Kravica warehouse your position was on the road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: In my estimate, maybe a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know who, if anyone, was deployed in front of the Kravica warehouse, along that segment of the road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, going in the other direction, towards Konjevic Polje, can you estimate how far you personally were located from the village of Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I said that a moment ago. I was right on the line dividing Sandici village from Kravica village, on a stretch of about a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. But can you offer the Court any estimate of how far you actually were from the village of Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's all right, sir. I'll move on. Do you recall the names of any colleagues who were deployed near you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you share them with the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Members of the 2nd Detachment, same as myself, Predrag Celic, Slobodan Stjepanovic, Ljubisa Becarevic, they were the closest to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you aware of or did you become informed about any other police or VRS forces who were also deployed along the road between Kravica, Sandici, towards Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what that unit or those units were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I remember first there was a special unit of the police from the Zvornik centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when we speak of a special unit of the police from the Zvornik centre, are we speaking of a PJP unit, as they are sometimes referred to, comprised of municipal policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, PJP, a Special Police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during the time when you were deployed along the road, did you personally see any Muslims surrender?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From my vantage point, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims at all while you were deployed there along the road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: You mean those people who were surrendering?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, I just asked you whether you personally saw anyone surrendering and your answer was "no," so I'm asking you did you see any Muslims at all in the area or passing through the area, be they soldiers or civilians.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber what you saw.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I saw motorcades of buses carrying civilians towards Konjevic Polje, and further down the road. I don't know where they were taking them. Women, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And while you were deployed along that road, did you hear any communication from the soldiers on the road to the Muslims in the woods?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was audible over the public address system, Muslims were being called upon to come down from the woods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, we are on 12th here, are we not? Just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I can clarify that, Your Honour. I'll just leave it at that. I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what day you heard this calling out? Actually let me withdraw that question because -- oh, no, you did answer the question. I see. Do you recall what day it was when you heard this calling out to the Muslims? Was it the 12th, the first day you were there, or was it another day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I cannot be sure about the date, but I heard the calling out. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you remember at all any details of what was being said by the soldiers to the Muslims when they were calling them to surrender?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: They were calling out to them to come down, to surrender. I believe the UNPROFOR was mentioned as being there. That's all I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, while you were deployed along that road, were you ever able to hear a Praga being fired? And if so, can you recall whether it was the first day you were there or another day, or more than one day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. That could be heard. I can't remember, maybe the second day we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And could you just describe generally from what area did it sound like to you it was being fired from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There was shooting, there was shooting, yes. Also to the left of Sandici village, there was sporadic shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So let me just see if I can make this a little simpler. When you were hearing the Pragas being fired, are you saying that it sounded like it was coming from the area of Sandici, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that the Praga was fired. I said one could hear shooting from Sandici downwards towards Konjevic Polje. There was shooting in the forest, where the Muslims were expected to come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then let me go back to my initial question on this topic a couple of questions ago, just to make sure I understand you correctly. During your deployment along that road, did you ever hear a Praga being fired?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the general area or location -- don't need a specific point, but just the general location or direction in which you heard -- you believe you heard that Praga being fired. For example, was it closer to Kravica or was it in the direction of Konjevic Polje? That's all I'm asking you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was closer to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, at some point when you were deployed on that road, did Mr. Cuturic come by your position and order you to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber that encounter with Mr. Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cuturic, the commander, came by in his car, in his vehicle, and if I remember correctly, he told us that a large group of Muslims was either expected to surrender or had already surrendered, so we should move and not stand on the road itself so that they can pass through, those who were going from the agricultural cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I see that your answer on the transcript ends with referring to "those who were going from the agricultural cooperative." Can you tell the Trial Chamber where Mr. Cuturic told you those Muslim prisoners, who had either surrendered or were expected to surrender, were going to be taken?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He said that they were about to pass by that road, from the agricultural cooperative on the way to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir -- and I'm looking at my colleagues here -- we may have a translation issue here. And I'll again try to make it as simple as I can. Mr. Cuturic advised you that the roads were going to be kept clear so that a large group of prisoners could be escorted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. A large group of Muslims who had surrendered or were about to surrender; that bit I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from what direction were those Muslims going to be escorted, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From Sandici towards the agricultural cooperative based in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what was the final destination of these prisoners that Mr. Cuturic told you? Where were they physically going to be taken finally, when he spoke to you at that time? Where were they going to be held?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He said they were going to be taken to that agricultural cooperative. I don't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think we've resolved the confusion. Thank you, sir. Now, did Mr. Cuturic, on this occasion, give you any further instructions, you personally?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. To me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what did he order you to do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: To come with him in his car, and after that he transferred me to the place called yellow bridge near Kravica, he gave me his Motorola and told me that he would let me know when those Muslims who had surrendered set off so that I can stop the convoy of buses carrying Muslim civilians, women, children, so that the Muslims who had surrendered could pass unhindered from Sandici towards the agricultural cooperative in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just ask you a couple of follow-up questions for clarification, sir. The convoy of buses that were carrying the Muslim civilians, from which direction were they travelling, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: They were coming from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when Mr. Cuturic picked you up in his vehicle and drove you to this location called Yellow Bridge, in what direction were you travelling at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: In the direction of Kravica, in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to be clear, we've heard earlier today, and throughout this trial already, references to the Zuti Most, that is above the UN base in Potocari. This Yellow Bridge that you've just referred to in Kravica is a different location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I understand there are a lot of Yellow Bridges in Bosnia, right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you said that Mr. Cuturic gave you, and it was translated as "his" Motorola. Was it your understanding that he was giving you his personal communication set or was he giving you another one for you to use?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The second Motorola, yes, another Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And presumably that is how he expected you to communicate with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall what your radio call sign was, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I seem to remember it was GRK, G-R-K.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was that short for anything?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Doesn't mean anything. It's just a call sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what Mr. Cuturic's call sign was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did he use?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Same as his nickname, Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall any other call signs being used during this period?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber any other call signs that you remember being used over the radio during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From what I was able to hear, and from what I remember, there was one call sign Bor, BOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to whom did that call sign belong, sir, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovcanin, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, during this period of time, sir, who else in your detachment had Motorolas? Who was issued them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Platoon commanders and the commander, the detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from whom was Mr. Cuturic receiving his orders during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know, probably from his superior commander, but I wouldn't know who.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, based on your service and your experience in the Special Police Brigade, who was in a position to issue Mr. Cuturic orders?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander, the brigade commander's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see we're nearing the break. I'm about to enter a new area, if I could suggest we take it a couple minutes early, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We can have a 25-minute break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just before we broke, you had testified that you were now posted at this area in Kravica known as Yellow Bridge, with a Motorola issued to you by Mr. Cuturic, and that he had told you to await his radio call in order that you would hold up a convoy of civilians from the direction of Bratunac. Did you receive such a further radio call from Mr. Cuturic, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, over the Motorola, he told me to hold up the convoy so that the Muslims who had surrendered to pass through to the agricultural cooperative in Kravica from the direction of Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did such a convoy arrive, sir? And if so, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The convoy arrived, yes. I came out, I stood in the road, I stopped the first bus, it came to a halt.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, after you stopped this bus, this convoy, what do you recall happening next?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. It stopped and then from the direction of Sandici, you could hear shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've already described in your testimony earlier today that there was shooting happening in general along this road, sometimes from the woods, sometimes from other locations. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what, if anything, was different about the shooting that you began to hear after you had stopped the convoy of civilians from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, this shooting that could be heard, well, it sounded as if it was closer to Sandici, in the direction of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. When you say it was closer to Sandici, in the direction of Kravica, does that mean it was closer to your location, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, closer to Kravica, in relation to Sandici. It was in the direction of Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what if anything was different about the nature of this shooting that you were now hearing, that sounded like it was closer to Kravica, closer to your location, than the shooting that you had been hearing earlier? Please take your time and answer the question as carefully as you can, sir. What was different about the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was more intense, and how should I put it? It seemed as if fire was being opened from one side alone. That was the impression that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you hear any radio traffic over your Motorola after the shooting started?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I heard our commander, Mr. Oficir, calling out names and informing someone that something had happened. He said that the hairpin had happened, that something had happened, that someone had been wounded or someone had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir, when you refer to hair pin, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It means that someone, in this case the officer, the commander, is informing someone, a superior officer, about the fact that someone was killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall Mr. Cuturic using anyone else's call sign during this conversation, this radio communication, you were hearing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Bor. I think he called out the name Bor. He called Bor.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, the officer Cuturic came in his vehicle, he came to where I was, by the Zuti Most. I stopped for a while, I saw that one of his arms was bandaged, I can't remember exactly. Very briefly he told me about what had happened down there, in front of the agricultural cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, from what direction was Mr. Cuturic travelling when he arrived at your position at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He arrived from the direction of Sandici. He was heading in the direction of Kravica, in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was he driving a detachment vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in the car?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber, in as much detail as you can, what Mr. Cuturic told you had happened back at the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, he said that the Muslims had taken away Krle's rifle, a member of the 3rd Platoon, and they used his rifle to kill him. There was shooting then, and he said he was going to Bratunac to the health centre. He said I should stay where I was until he returned and issued other orders. He said he had burnt himself because he got hold of the barrel of a rifle, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I note that the transcript didn't capture the name of the member of the 3rd Platoon who had his rifle taken away, according to Mr. Cuturic. Can you just repeat the name of the man who was killed, whose rifle had been taken away from him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: His nickname was Krle but his name was Krsto. I don't know his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know where Krsto was from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I know he was from Skelani and that he was a member of the 3rd Skelani Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, while Mr. Cuturic was telling you all this, was the shooting still going on, this new shooting, this different shooting that you were hearing? Was it still going on?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. You could still here the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, did you ask Mr. Cuturic what was happening to the Muslim prisoners back in the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember asking him about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember him telling you, during this conversation while you heard this shooting going on, what was happening to the Muslim prisoners back in the Kravica warehouse, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, he told me about what had happened. He said he was going to Bratunac. He said that they were shooting at Muslims, but I can't remember everything he said, all his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question, sir, is did he tell you what was happening to the Muslims at the time, the same time you were speaking to him? Did he tell you what was happening to them down in the warehouse? Not what had happened beforehand but what was happening as you were speaking to him and hearing the shooting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, that's asked and answered and if the Prosecution wants this witness to try to explain what was happening at the time that the third party was not even at the warehouse is impossible. So I object on those grounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, do you wish to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think my questions having pretty clear and I don't believe he has fully answered the question I asked, so I'm following up with a simple question about what Mr. Cuturic told him, if anything, was happening to those prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection overturned. We are of the opinion that Mr. Thayer's last question is a step further from his previous question, so please proceed. You may, of course, repeat the question if you wish to, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Otherwise I can read it out myself to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll just give it another try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, on this occasion, when Mr. Cuturic was telling you what had happened back at the warehouse, and how he injured his hand, while you were hearing the shooting going on still from that area, what did he tell you, if anything, was still going on with respect to those Muslim prisoners back at the warehouse? What, if anything, did he tell you was happening to them as he was speaking to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that they had started shooting at the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question isn't whether they had started shooting. My question is, sir, what if anything did he tell you was still going on at the time you were speaking to him at Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, I think it's been asked and answered now twice at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The problem is with the word "started." One moment. Let me confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer has every good reason to proceed along with the questions that he's been putting because the witness has used the word "started." You can only start at one given moment, and as you proceed, you are no longer starting, you are continuing. So I think the question that Mr. Thayer put to you should be answered by you. At a certain time, Mr. Cuturic, Oficir, was supposedly, according to Mr. Thayer, telling you what was happening. What did he tell you was happening then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he said that they were shooting at the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I'll proceed, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. He's your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cuturic change your assignment at all with these new developments?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question: Is this Mr. Cuturic still alive or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've had previous testimony to that effect, and I can certainly put that question to the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you heard His Honour's question. Do you know whether or not Mr. Cuturic is still living?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He's not alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when he died?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He was killed on Ozren. I know that, but I don't know the exact date. I don't know the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And after your conversation with Mr. Cuturic at Zuti Most, in what direction did he head at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He set off in the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you continue to hold up that convoy, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did the shooting continue, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did Oficir return, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what, if anything, he said to you when he passed back through your position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember whether he stopped when he returned. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from which direction was he travelling when he returned to your position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac, because that's the direction he had set off in.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when he returned from the direction of Bratunac, was there anyone else in the car with him?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. When he set off, there was no one, but I can't remember when he returned and whether there was anyone with him either.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So please tell the Trial Chamber what happened next, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: After a while I was ordered by Commander Cuturic to let the convoy pass through. He said it could pass through and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did the shooting stop after Mr. Cuturic passed back through your position, coming from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall approximately what time of the day it was when the shooting finally stopped? I'm not asking you for a watch time, just what time of the day, if you can recall, it was when the shooting finally stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime in the afternoon, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would this be early, mid or late afternoon, sir, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was in the late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What happened next, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: When he told me the convoy could pass through, he also told me to stay at that location, at Zuti Most, and he said that the bus that had brought us there from our detachment would be arriving from the direction of Kravica or Bratunac, and he said I should get on the bus and go to Konjevic Polje and continue in the direction of Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection approximately how long it was before this bus arrived, from the time you spoke last with Mr. Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember how much time passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you this, sir: By the time the shooting had stopped, was it dark yet?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. Perhaps it was dusk, but it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when this bus arrived for you, sir, was it the actual detachment bus, the official bus?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And other than the driver, was there anyone else on the bus when it picked you up?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, could you kindly ask him again from what direction did the bus come at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, from what direction did this bus come to fetch you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac, Bratunac, Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he may have -- you may need sometime but for me I have difficulty to find out the exact place of Zuti Most, so sometime if you could ask him to mark on the map the place where he stopped the buses, the buses of convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll try to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We didn't have much luck with sketches and maps, Your Honour, but I'll do my best with what we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A rough whereabouts of Zuti Most in relation to Kravica, Sandici, Bratunac, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. With the Court's indulgence let me just identify a map that we can perhaps call up on e-court, and we can answer Your Honour's question right away. If we may have map 6 of the Court binder map book, ERN 05054371, I think we'll be able to call that up. That's 65 ter 2111. And if we could focus, it will be the top third of the map on the location depicting the road running between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje. That is what we will be showing the witness. That's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see a map in front of you on your computer screen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I just want you to take a moment and orient yourself, if you would. Do you recognise the various locations that are depicted along that communication between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to take the magic pen that Madam Usher is about to hand you and mark - and we understand that this is not going to be exact - the approximate location, and please do this with an X, of this area called Zuti Most, where you were posted by Mr. Cuturic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Zuti Most was in the village of Kravica, not far from the coach station. Kravica is an inhabited place and it's on the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And in your recollection, it was actually located within the village of Kravica, is that your testimony? Not outside on one side or the other but within the physical confines of the village of Kravica; is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The village of Kravica is spread along the road to a certain extent, in the direction of Sandici, but most of the inhabitants are in the village of Kravica, but the Zuti Most location is at the exit of the coach station. It wasn't in fact Zuti Most, it was subsequently built. There was a fence that was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And was it closer to Bratunac or closer to Konjevic Polje, in the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere there, in the middle, because Kravica is in the middle of this section of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Then why don't we just put an X right where the area of Kravica is depicted? That little circle right under Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we really need that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What I'd like to know actually is that -- in relation to the location of that warehouse, whether his place is located to the direction of Bratunac or on the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's precisely what my next question is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you mark with another circle the approximate location of the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Looking from Kravica, it was towards Sandici, perhaps some 700 metres from this Yellow Bridge, in my estimate. That would be about here. [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when the bus came to fetch you, sir, from which direction was the bus travelling?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Bratunac. That's the junction between Kravica and Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So it was coming from the right-hand side as depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because Judge Kwon rightly is pointing out to me that we could have later on some confusion when trying to read into this map. There is an X there that the witness marked. You had actually asked him to mark with a circle the approximate location of the Kravica warehouse. Now, he didn't mark anything with a circle. He marked -- he put an X. So if he could perhaps tell us now what that X represents, because I want to make sure that there will not be any confusion later on, and then he needs to mark also his own location. What does that X that you marked on the map indicate, Mr. Pepic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, sir, instead of the circle the Prosecutor told me to put, I put an X but I can correct it if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not important that you correct it. What is important is that you tell us what that X represents. Does it represent the Kravica warehouse? Or does it represent the spot where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is the warehouse of the agricultural cooperative in Kravica. But I just put an X instead of a circle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And could you now indicate -- first let's start like this. First, beneath that X, could you put the letters KW?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need no assist him. Okay. All right. That's good. Now, we need you to mark with another X, on that same map, the spot where you were. Did you understand me, Mr. Pepic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did, but there is a yellow dot here and I'm trying to put my X on top of it but I'm not managing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Then we give you another magic pen with a different colour and you can indicate the spot where you were with a different colour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Next to it, to its right, could you please put MP, Milenko Pepic, MP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the bus to fetch you arrived from what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we need this map any further, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Pepic, at the top right-hand corner of the map, if you could kindly put your initials or signature, and today's date? Today is the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Pepic. And that can be archived. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit number IC 137.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, after this bus picked you up, what direction did you head?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From Kravica to Sandici and on to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So did you pass the Kravica warehouse on your way to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what, if anything, you noticed about the Kravica warehouse as you drove by in the bus?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I noticed on the wall of the cooperative there were visible traces of bullets, and outside the cooperative there was a pile of hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, first of all, with respect to the bullet holes you saw, sir, can you describe generally for the Trial Chamber the quantity of bullet holes that you saw? I'm not asking to you count them but just can you give the Trial Chamber an idea of the number?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, there were obvious, obvious bullet holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was it a few, a lot?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, quite a few, quite a few. Large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were those bullet holes present on the outside of the Kravica warehouse when you had passed by the previous day, or when you had first been deployed to that location?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Not that I had noticed, but I didn't look.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this hay that you've described, sir, why does the hay stand out in your mind?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, when I was going from Sandici towards Kravica, I hadn't noticed it. I hadn't noticed that hay piled up.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At this time, if we may have 65 ter number 1563 displayed on e-court? Sir, do you see an image on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the structures in this image?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Across the road from the building.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Across the road there is this building of the agricultural cooperative. MR.THAYER:

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would take that pen, sir, and just write ZZ on the roof of that building you've identified as the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, there is more than one warehouse. I see four. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well the one where you saw the hay being laid out and the bullet holes, that's the one we are talking about. Is that the one you just marked with ZZ?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you just circle, sir, the area where you saw this hay piled up outside the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks] This area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you recall where you saw the bullet holes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, on this wall, all over this wall where the hay was, that wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you just mark with an X the wall you're referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I see you've marked it with three Xs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. That part of the wall is where I noticed those bullet holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I'd just ask you to write your initials in the lower right-hand corner and today's date, which is the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we can save the exhibit, please, and we'll be done with it. Sir, do you recall seeing any bodies in front of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't. I just saw the hay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing any soldiers in front of the warehouse as you drove by on your way to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were they in uniform, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you make out what unit they belonged to or even whether they were police or army?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell. I didn't know that [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you arrived at Konjevic Polje, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: When we got to Konjevic Polje, we headed to the right, towards Zvornik, and that's where we were billeted in abandoned Muslim houses to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
