utterances.text: Just one very small intervention, in the transcript, if I remember the answer that witness gave, it's on page 44, line 18, he answered, "I didn't know them" and here it says, "I didn't know that." Meaning that he didn't know the soldiers that he saw in front of the warehouse so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a fairly legitimate point that you make, and I think we need to address it to the witness also because the question itself was a little bit compound. Now, let's start with the first question, Mr. Pepic. Could you make out what or which unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could you at least make out whether they belonged to the police or whether they belonged to the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does that satisfy you, Mr. Lazarevic? And you, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, before we talk about what happened when you were at the abandoned house in Konjevic Polje, while you were deployed along the road, either at the retaining wall where you were positioned, or at Zuti Most, did anyone tell you or did you hear that General Mladic was in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I heard he was around in those parts. But I didn't see him myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, while you were deployed along the road, again either at your position at the retaining wall or later when you were posted at Zuti Most, did anyone tell you or did you hear that Mr. Borovcanin was in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I did hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you were posted at the Zuti Most location, do you recall ever seeing Mr. Borovcanin pass by your position?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see him at all when you were posted on that road, either at the retaining wall or at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, back to the houses, sir, at Konjevic Polje, who was with you in the abandoned house?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: My fellow members of the same platoon, Predrag Celic, Zoran Vukic, Zoran Tomic. There were those of us that I can remember. Zoran Lukic actually, not Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Cuturic while you were staying in that house?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. He stopped by and stayed very briefly with us at the abandoned house.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what if anything did he tell you at the time he stopped by? And again please think carefully, sir, and try to remember to the best of your recollection exactly what Mr. Cuturic told you when he came by that house.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he told us what had happened to our colleague named Krle, K-R-L-E, how it came about that he was wounded, and that's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything at all about the people who did the shooting at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything at all what he thought would happen to the people who did the shooting at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't understand this question. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Cuturic express to you any opinion about what would or should happen to whoever committed the shootings in the Kravica warehouse, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, he said, "Somebody will have to be held accountable for what had happened at the cooperative in Kravica, sooner or later." That's what I remember him saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you and your colleagues discuss who was responsible for the shooting at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. Not that I remember. We didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, did you ever try to find out who did?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To this day, sir, do you have any information as to who did the shooting at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you spend the night in that abandoned house in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you know how many days and nights you actually spent deployed along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: You mean the road, Bratunac-Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir, before you spent the night in that abandoned house.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I couldn't recall. I remember -- if I remember well -- in the evening on the 11th, we were put up at Bjelovac, that's one night, and I remember the night in Konjevic Polje, and later on, further down the road to Zvornik. I cannot get the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And did I show you some medical records from the Bratunac medical centre yesterday when we met, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber what those medical records showed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Medical files from the health centre in Bratunac, if I understood correctly, with records of the time and date when the gentleman nicknamed Oficir was at the health centre and when our other colleague, Krle, was brought to Bratunac to the health centre. It also lists the injuries on Mr. Cuturic, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what the date was on those entries for those two patients, when they were admitted to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: 13th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you saw that record, sir, did that jog your memory or did that help your recollection at all as to how many nights you may have spent along the road before you spent the night in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Most probably only one night, the night of the 12th. That could be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, sir, in your recollection, were you posted at Zuti Most by Mr. Cuturic and then withdrawn to Konjevic Polje, to those houses, on the same day, whatever the date was of that day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So where were you deployed next from Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were sent off, if I remember correctly, in the direction of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you deployed to any particular location in the Zvornik area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From what I remember, from Zvornik we were sent on to Baljkovica. Baljkovica is a village not far from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how much time you spent in the Baljkovica area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: One night, we spent there. That's something I remember. And the next day we stayed on for a while but until when, I can't remember. We left maybe in the afternoon most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And while were you deployed to that area, was there fighting, was there combat?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: You mean in Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe the nature of the fighting, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Infantry combat, shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did the Serb forces suffer killed and wounded during those engagements?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that. Some were wounded, some were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that Mr. Cuturic told you that someone would be held accountable for what happened at the Kravica warehouse. Did any superior officer in the Special Police Brigade ever ask you for a report concerning your actions or your platoon's actions along that road in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever do so, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions at this time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Who is going first? Mr. Stojanovic? If could you kindly introduce yourself with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Good day to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, my name is Stojanovic and together with my colleagues, I represent Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin. I was following your testimony and now I'll just try to go through some of the questions to which I believe some of the answers were unclear. Let's try and establish a chronology of events because I'm under the impression that we have a problem when it comes to certain dates, certain dates that are very important for us. Would you agree with me if I said that on the 11th of July, in the afternoon, you set off from the Sarajevo battlefield in the direction of Bratunac and the village of Bjelovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your unit was transferred on that occasion by bus, and lorry. These were buses and lorry that your unit had at that time in July of 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection how many members of the Sekovici Detachment approximately arrived in the Bratunac area on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number but there were two platoons or rather there were three infantry platoons, as far as I can remember, but as far as the strength of the troops is concerned, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that a police platoon within a detachment has about 30 men?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, more or less, sometimes there were fewer men. Between 20 and 30 men, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Bratunac, you did not know what your future combat task would be at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time upon arriving in Bratunac or, rather, in the place called Bjelovac, which you spent the night, did you at any point in time receive information according to which the Republika Srpska army had entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, we heard that on the 11th, there was Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are following the transcript, the sentence isn't complete. I'll put the question to you again and you can answer it by saying yes or no. At any point in time upon arriving in Bratunac, did you receive information according to which Republika Srpska troops had already entered Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go in chronological order. Between the 9th of the [as interpreted] -- and the 11th and 12th, you spent that night in the school in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: For the sake of the transcript, let's repeat this because on page 52, line 2 and 3, I don't think it has been correctly recorded. So would we agree that the night between the 11th and 12th of July was a night that you spent in that school in Bjelovac, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, you received your first combat assignment, and that was to turn right from the Zuti Most down towards the villages that you could see in front of you; if you're looking in the direction of Potocari, that was the direction you had to head in; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether you received any concrete order that had to do with the UN check-point that was by the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, we hadn't received any orders about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember whether there was a UN check-point on the other side of the Zuti Most, if you're looking in the direction of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember having seen such a check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Given my understanding of your answers provided today and the way you understood your first task on the 12th of July, was that you should search the terrain and perhaps engage in combat with any enemy forces that might be present in the area. Is my conclusion correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have already told us that you did not have any concrete orders that concerned encounters with the civilian population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also said when carrying out the combat task you didn't encounter any ABiH members. You also didn't see any civilians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Had you encountered any civilians, you assume you would have asked your superior officers for instructions as to what to do; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in time you received an order, as you said two or three hours after you had been advancing towards these villages, you received the order to return to the asphalt road leading from Bratunac to Potocari. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you reached the asphalt road not far from the Zuti Most; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please assist us now and let's have a look at Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 4D101, Your Honours. This is a map of the area. We have already used this map when another Prosecution witness appeared here. Mr. Pepic, while we are waiting for the map to appear on the monitor, I'll just say that this is a map of the area you have been referring to. I will soon ask you to mark the locations you have been mentioning. If we can scroll down a bit and go to the left, scroll down a little more or perhaps scroll up a bit. Yes. That's -- scroll up a little more. No, in the other direction. I apologise. Scroll down. A little more. Thank you. I think that will be fine. Could we perhaps zoom in a little? Just a little. And scroll down a little more so that we can see this area. That's excellent. Thanks. Could the usher please provide the witness with the marker we will be using to mark certain locations on the map? Mr. Pepic, can you find your bearings on this map now? If you can see the road from Bratunac to Potocari, it's marked in yellow, isn't it? And behind a place called Borici, there is a point at which the road is cut off or interrupted. I don't know if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It's not very clear. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Follow the road marked in yellow, the road to Potocari, and you'll find a place marked the village of Borici?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Go further down and at the location marked P 60/6, can you see this cut off point?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this might represent the bridge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You can also see the river there, the point at which it crosses the river?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Knjisi [phoen] river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you think it's better, I was going to suggest that we could zoom in that particular part to which you have referred the witness, particularly where there is Borici and where there is exactly -- yes. You can zoom even further. We can zoom even further. Yes, and I think the witness himself can have a second look and probably will be in a position to confirm his previous answers, wouldn't you, Mr. Pepic? And then we can proceed. Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the villages to the right of the road. The villages Budak and Pale, can you see them?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, try and mark the route you followed more or less when you went to the right of the road and mark the circle in the direction of the village and can you also mark the point where you reached the road, the asphalt road, more or less?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, we have the Zuti Most, the Yellow Bridge here, and we set off to the right from this location. [Marks] The closest village here is Budak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you then follow this road that's marked here to descend to the -- into the main road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember, we followed the same route.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you use the red marker to indicate the route you took to get down to the asphalt road from this dirt road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was like this. [Marks] It was in the vicinity of the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we agree that this was on the 12th of July 1995, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you for something else. Could you just mark the starting point with the letter A, the point from which you set off?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And could we agree that you turned right below the bridge when you're looking in the direction of Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this because given the map we could have the impression that you set off in the direction behind the bridge. Please mark with the letter B the point at which you reached the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The witness has marked those two sites. Now could you just write down the date, the 9th of July 2007, and could you put your initials on the document anywhere to the right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, could we zoom in again for another two questions and then I won't need the map, but now we could remove it because I don't need it in this form any more.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Could we in fact zoom out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are going to store this first, Mr. Stojanovic. Then we'll get the same map. Do you wish us to zoom in further or zoom out? Out? Okay. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we just zoom out and then store this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. First we store this and then we zoom out. So let's store this, please, and then give it the number later. We will communicate that to the parties. Is it stored?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we can have the same map without these markings. Yes, okay. And we can zoom out. You tell us when to stop, Mr. Stojanovic. Because I don't know what your intentions are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is quite enough, Your Honour. We now have an idea where Potocari is in view of the next two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, would you now agree that, now that we have seen what you've marked, that the spot where you emerged on the asphalt road and where relative to the position where you saw civilians in the industrial zone in Potocari, the distance was at least 1500 metres between these two?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You, and the members of your unit, never approached the industrial zone of Potocari where the refugees were, not at any moment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that you left this area before the evacuation of these people began, towards Kladanj and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: None of the members of your unit had any specific assignment related to organising the evacuation of refugees from Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you then returned to the Yellow Bridge, boarded your own bus, and went towards Bratunac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point, on the way towards Zvornik, you stopped in the area of Sandici village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. We stopped before Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us try to reconstruct the chronology of events. You said it was sometime in the afternoon. Can we then agree it was in the afternoon of the 12th July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will try to establish a time line to make it easier for all of us. It is the claim of this Defence that your next assignment was to secure the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje and to defend Kravica and Sandici from possible breakout attempts by Muslim forces. Was that your understanding as well of your next combat assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: By the way, let me ask you, in view of what you answered to my colleague, Mr. Thayer, in all those numerous combat assignments all over Republika Srpska, to the best of your knowledge, did your unit ever use megaphones?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, again to the best of your knowledge, that your unit did not possess any megaphones to use for such purposes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't have megaphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A number of questions were asked here in attempts to establish where you were in the afternoon of the 12th. Would you agree with me if I said that you personally were on the border between Sandici village and Kravica village, not far from the road sign that marks the beginning of the area of Sandici? Is that correct? Is that the correct description of the location where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In examination-in-chief you gave an estimate of 1.000 metres as the distance to the warehouse in Kravica, but I would like to ask you how far were you from the house that was on the slope above you in the area that we call Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Up to 500 metres, maybe a little more or a little less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer? Sorry, I was looking at you. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just have some more clarification as to the approximate location of this house, I don't believe we've heard any testimony about it. If my friend is going there, I apologise for intervening. I just wanted to get some orientation as to this house on the slope because there are a number of houses that have been referred to with respect to these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you do that, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think we will clarify this and we are just about to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, to the best of your recollection of that period, and I suppose you know the area well because you still live and work there, do you remember there was an elevation there, in the area that we call Sandici village, there was a destroyed house in the direction of Kravica looking from Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, when you answered that in your rough estimate you were about 500 metres away from it, was that the house you meant?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we should be having a break in a couple of minutes' time. Whenever it's convenient for you, we'll have it, we will have the break. Go ahead. Go on, if you need another two minutes before you move on to the next topic. Otherwise we stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe this is a good moment to break because I'm moving to the next day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's what I felt. That's why I asked you. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President if we could just have a rough estimate on how much longer my friend has? We have another witness that's waiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, the latest update that we had was one hour for the Borovcanin team, and that was this morning, correct me if I am wrong, and then we have about another hour and a half distributed amongst the other Defence teams. We can verify that. Mr. Zivanovic, do you still need 20 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we will not have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I believe we probably will have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Nikolic has already indicated that there is no intention to cross-examine this witness. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau? You requested 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we'll probably have no questions at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. The Gvero team no questions. Thank you, Madam Fauveau. And the Pandurevic team, 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Less than five.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Less than five. All right. And you, Mr. Stojanovic, how much more? You had asked for one hour. I know you always feel confused when I put this question to you but please do give us an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we have stuck quite closely to our estimate. We have used up half an hour already, and from the remaining questions, I think we'll need just another half hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And do you plan to have a re-examination with this witness so far, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Not so far, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not so far. So basically after the break, we'll have roughly three-quarters of an hour, two-thirds of which will be taken by Mr. Stojanovic, I take it, another five minutes by Mr. Haynes a bit more or less. So if we can start with the next witness, say, for ten minutes -- but at best, at best, we could have him for about ten minutes max, so please you take the decision on what you think you ought to do. We'll have a 25-minute break from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey, before we rise, there is a Borovcanin motion for certification for purposes of our videolink decision which we handed down last week. We would like you to you file your response to it by not later than by the end of this week, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May I just have two minutes of your attention? My team is finalising our submission concerning the analysis of intercepts, and our submission would be longer than the 3.000 words envisaged by the directive on written submissions. It's a general analysis of all the intercepts used in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You want that limit extended, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can decide on that here and now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So how much more do you require, roughly?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is hard to say at this moment, but I believe that we will need more than double.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Try to restrict it to double, please. And to that extent, we are prepared to grant you. Yes. We grant your request.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may just to let the Court know, we decided to send the next witness home for the day, just given our experience and how things generally turn out, we thought it would be on the whole better just to call him back and begin tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think we will be utilising the entire time in any case. Thank you for keeping us informed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are going to continue. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, if you recall, we left off discussing the afternoon of the 12th of July and the location where you were standing on the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that practically that evening of the 12th of July and the night of the 12th of July, you spent there on the road because on the 13th, as you put it, the next day, you received a new assignment to hold up traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how the events unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We dispose of information - and I can even tell you who told us this - that that night of the 12th, the BH army attacked this road and on that occasion a member of the 1st Company of PJP, Zeljko Nikolic, was killed, while three members of the police were wounded. Could you confirm this to the best of your recollection, and can you confirm that there was indeed fighting that night with the armed forces of the BH?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about the death of this colleague from PJP on that section of the road towards Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that those two days, the afternoon of the 12th and the day of the 13th, you saw UN vehicles escorting the civilian convoys heading to Kladanj and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to jog your memory. Do you remember seeing an armoured personnel carrier with the emblem of the UN on that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember the APC, but I don't know on which of the two days I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But you can confirm today that it was on one of these two days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And if our time line is correct, we are now coming to the next day when you were again on the road, that afternoon you received an assignment from the commander of your unit to hold up traffic on that road, is this consistent with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree for the record that that could be the 13th of July, the afternoon of the 13th?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When my learned friend Mr. Thayer examined you, you said the reason why you were supposed to hold up traffic was what your commander told you, namely that a group of Muslims was about to surrender and they were about to pass by that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said the Muslims were supposed to surrender. Do you know when they surrendered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Nor do you know to which unit they surrendered?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that it was not your unit to which they surrendered because otherwise you would have known?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There were no Muslims surrendering on the section of the road where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that on that day, the traffic on the road was intensive? On one hand, there were convoys of trucks and buses and passenger cars and combat vehicles from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, while the transports of Muslims were supposed to be in the opposite direction and that could have caused a collapse in traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it precisely in order to avoid that that you understood you were given that order by your commander to hold up traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your assignment was to stop all traffic on the road at the moment when the transfer of captured Muslims was to take place towards Kravica. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The place that you called Zuti Most, the place that you marked, is at least 700 metres in your assessment from the warehouse in Kravica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's physically impossible to see the warehouse in Kravica from that location?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did you have to wait until your commander came in that vehicle? How much time passed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I couldn't answer. Can't remember how much time passed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could just clarify which time we are talking about. There were a couple of encounters and conversations with Mr. Cuturic. I just want to make that clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please address that, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was as follows: How much time passed from the time you arrived at Zuti Most up until the time you saw Rade Cuturic, your commander, going in the direction of Bratunac, with his arms that were bandaged as you yourself have already said? Your answer was that you can't assess the time that passed.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's been cleared up now. While you were on the bridge, you said that you heard shooting from the direction of Sandici and from various positions. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you said that at one point in time you heard intense firing that continued for up to an hour. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When Rade Cuturic your commander arrived with his bandaged arm and was heading towards Bratunac, this intensive firing stopped and you could hear firing that was less intensive from the direction of Sandici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time, and from the same direction, from the direction of Konjevic Polje, towards Bratunac, did you see some other vehicle in front of or behind the vehicle that Rade Cuturic was in?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you can't remember, does that mean that perhaps some other vehicle passed by, but you cannot remember that now?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps some other vehicle did pass by, but I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing any dead member of your unit being transported to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't show the document that you were shown initially and the document Mr. Thayer referred to, but if you remember it's a report from the health centre in Bratunac and it says the 13th of July at 1645, Dragicevic, Krsto, was taken there, he was dead, and Rade Cuturic also appeared, he had been wounded, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could we agree that it's logical to assume that when Rade Cuturic went to Bratunac, this was probably before 1645? That would be a logical conclusion, and it was on the 13th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You also remember that at one point in time, Rado Cuturic, your commander, went from Bratunac to Konjevic Polje, and he was alone in the vehicle on that occasion too, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Given what we have just said about the time and given that you've said that it was in the afternoon on the 13th of July, as far as you can remember, would you say that it was between or rather around 1800 hours?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned passing by the Kravica warehouse, you said that from the bus you were in you could see some soldiers in front of the warehouse. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know which unit they were members of?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You are only sure that they weren't members of your own unit because had they been from your unit, you would have recognised them, you knew your comrades in arms and your colleagues; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you're certain that they were not members of your unit; can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's pay attention to the chronological events. Between 2000 and 2100 hours, on the 13th of July, that evening, you left the area, set off in the direction of Zvornik, and found accommodation in Konjevic Polje, is that what you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it was the night of the 13th, between the 13th and the 14th, and that is the night that you spent in Konjevic Polje, in those abandoned houses, can we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And during examination-in-chief you said that at one point in time, Rade Cuturic appeared in the house were you in, and he told you about the events that you have described in detail, in answer to Mr. Thayer's questions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Rado Cuturic tell you how it is that Dragicevic Krsto ended up in Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time, did you obtain information according to which Krsto Dragicevic went there to check whether any of his Muslim neighbours were there, neighbours he could ask about the fate of his brother or cousin who was killed in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't say. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether after these events, you had heard of such a reason for which Krsto went down there, so I'm not asking you about that evening, I'm asking you about whether you heard about this later.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't provide you with a precise answer but there was some relative of his that was killed and it's probably for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time after these events did you hear that anyone from your unit or from some other MUP unit participated in the shooting of these Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on that evening, the evening of the 13th, in Konjevic Polje, there were no members of the Skela platoon with you, there were only members of the Marko Aleksic platoon and of your platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, yes, that's correct, but now, as for the 3rd Platoon, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: By analysing your testimony, I realised that you practically can't remember that day, the 14th. You can't remember whether you moved or you stayed in that area, Konjevic Polje and Drinjaca river, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist because something similar happened with another witness, but let me ask you this: On the 15th of July, you arrived in Zvornik and it was a warm day, you were waiting in Zvornik for a new assignment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon of the 15th, you received orders to go to Baljkovica village, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You spent the night of the 15th on your positions in Baljkovica, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that you remember this because everybody who testified before you spoke about extremely inclement weather that night?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 16th, in the afternoon, when the column passed, the column of the 28th Division, you were told to be on ease and you received permission to take some rest and that's when you left this area, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, in conclusion, in broader terms than my colleague asked you before, from the 12th of July, when you arrived at the Yellow Bridge, until the afternoon of the 16th of July, when you got your leave, over those four days, did you personally see Ljubomir Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your unit travelled all over Republika Srpska on various combat assignments and on those assignments, the units were commanded by Ljubomir Borovcanin, were you there on such battlefields, on such assignments?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What are your impressions about him as a commanding officer, as a person, from that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I have only the best to say about our former commander. He was an honest man, he treated us all equally, without any favouritism or discrimination. All the best.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You still work as a policeman today, a member of the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You have been vetted by the European Union's observers mission?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: None of them ever indicated that in any indication -- that in any investigation into events related to Srebrenica, you were found responsible?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Witness. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes? Or Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: I am Djordje Sarapa, attorney at law appearing for the accused Pandurevic. I have a couple of questions for you regarding Baljkovica. You said a moment ago that you spent the night of the 15th on your positions in Baljkovica which means that on the 16th you were still on those positions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: On the 16th, you received orders to withdraw to the hill just before Baljkovica to allow the passage of the troops and Muslims going towards Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: You were told then that you were not to shoot because a cease-fire had been agreed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I seem to remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know that on that occasion, a large number of civilians and troops were allowed to pass through, and went on their way?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Just one question about your colleagues from your unit. Was anybody from the Sekovici Detachment wounded or killed at Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Some people were wounded, but I'm not sure about any killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Very briefly, Your Honour, just on one matter that arose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir I asked you generally about some medical records that we looked at yesterday and my friend also asked you some questions about those records. What I'd like to do is just go ahead and show you and have displayed a copy of those records on e-court. This is 65 ter 1892 and we're talking about page 30, I believe, of the document. It has previously come in as 4DP01892, so it may be in the system that way. And if I might have the assistance of Madam Usher it may be more helpful, sir, for you to look at the original of the log here, and I'll give that to you to look at. Perhaps we could -- I don't know if we can run that on ELMO at the same time. If we could just rotate that, please? Sir, do you see the entry that's marked as 1490 on the very left-most column?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you see a date and a time in the column immediately to the right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is the date and time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 13th of July 1995, 1740.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is the name that appears next to that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Cuturic, father's name Milan, Rade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next column has a date of birth; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The 26th of August, 1971.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does the next column say? What is the heading of that column? What is the information there? Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Address.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next column, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Unit. And then abbreviation, "Spec. MUP Brigade." Special MUP Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does the next column refer to? What's that heading?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Place where the individual was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what does it say there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It says Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to look down to the next entry marked 1491. Do you see a date and time listed? And it may or may not be more legible on the original. I just ask to you look at the original sir because it's not entirely clear on the computer here, sir. Can you see what the time is?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What does it look like to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: 13th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the time, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Is it a 9 or an 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And what is the name of the patient?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Krsto Dragicevic, father's name Bogoljub.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the year of birth is listed as 1965, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Address -- address, Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Next column is again Spec Policija Skelani, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the final column, what does that say there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Which final column? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: The one right next to Special Policija, Skelani?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, it's not the last one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place where the individual is wounded, it's Kravica as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in answer to a question from my colleague about whether or not you'd heard information that this Krsto or Krle, as you knew him, had a relative in Kravica, you answered that you didn't have that particular information, but you had heard that one of his relatives had been killed and you said that that was probably why he was there. When did you first hear this information, sir, that this Krle had a relative that may have been killed in this area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a brief digression, I do apologise to my colleague. On page 76, line 17, the question was that I asked the witness whether he was aware of the fact that the late Krsto had a relative who had been killed from Kravica. The question wasn't from Kravica. The question was from Skelani. I don't want to confuse the witness. So it was a relative from Skelani who died in 1993. It wasn't a relative from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Yes, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So my question, sir, is when did you first hear this information or rumour that this Krle had had a relative who was killed at Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say when exactly, but perhaps Krle himself said something about a relative of his in Skelani who had been killed. As to when this occurred, as to the year, I don't know, but it was during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember when you heard this information, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you ever shared this information with any investigators or lawyers prior to your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, did, to your knowledge, Mr. Cuturic have any relatives that had been killed in Kravica that you're aware of? Did you ever hear any information or rumours along those lines?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you also testified sir that you had no information about any of your detachment, in answer to a question from my friend, being involved in the shooting of the prisoners in the Kravica warehouse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the nature of the indictment in the case in which you testified in Sarajevo, which specifically charges members of your detachment with those killings?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that members of your detachment implicated themselves, that is confessed, that they participated in the shooting at the warehouse? Did you ever hear that information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this kind of question. This is factually incorrect. The trial before the BH court is ongoing, the Prosecution is presenting its case, so if any of the accused has confessed to this crime, well, this hasn't been achieved. All the accused from various units are still on trial. So for these reasons, I object to this form of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The position is we see plenty of value in the submission made by Mr. Stojanovic, especially since this is an ongoing trial, and therefore, insofar as you put a question which refers specifically to a trial and the witnesses' testimony in that trial being a trial that is still pending, I don't think it -- we don't believe that it is proper for you to proceed that way. However, you can ask the witness if he is aware, independently of this trial, and without reference to this trial, whether he is aware that some members of the detachment actually admitted to their participation in the events that you allege.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll leave your question right there and put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you understand His Honour's statement and the question that he put?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Then I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, since this document has been used could I just put one question that has to do with this document from the Bratunac health centre? It won't take me more than a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you want to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask the witness a question about this document from the health centre, and about the column that concerns another wounded individual who was delivered at the same time from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please tell us what the question is. You have stated that already. What is your question? And then we decide whether to allow it or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question would be: After we show him the document, whether he knows Miroslav Stanojevic and whether he knows that as a member of the Red Berets he was wounded in Kravica and taken there to the health centre in Bratunac on that very same day at 1730 hours. Perhaps he could just answer by saying yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Exceptionally, please, Mr. Pepic, if you could answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know Miroslav Stanojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it. That brings your testimony to an end, Mr. Pepic. I wish to thank you for having come over to give testimony, and on behalf of everyone I wish you a safe journey back home. We will reconvene tomorrow in the morning with the next witness. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, you will see that we have filed I believe two motions for protective measures. It's a relatively minor situation. For the next two witnesses. They both asked -- well, I'm sure the one that I've spoken to had asked for facial distortion only. The other one did in the last trial as well, so if we can confirm that we will be passing that on to you as well. I don't know if the Defence -- I've asked one or two of the Defences if they had any problem with it. It's measures they had in the last trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. In any case we'll have to decide that tomorrow. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
